title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, route53
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Add a reusable Terraform module and top-level deployment configuration to provision the Private Control Plane VPC topology required for Private deployments (multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, Route53 private hosted zones + resolver rules). This is the infra piece required for ENG-9451 and will be used by the private-installer and the Terraform examples in the docs.

What this PR does (checklist):
- [x] Add terraform/modules/control-plane-vpc: parameterized module for VPC, AZ subnets (public/private), NAT, route tables
- [x] Add terraform/modules/control-plane-endpoints: interface endpoints for S3/STS/SSM/EC2/SecretsManager used by the control plane
- [x] Add security group module and default rules used by control plane services
- [x] Add vpc peering and conditional peering attachment resources to connect a customer VPC to the control plane (with optional cross-account role)
- [x] Add Route53 private hosted zone creation and resolvers for cross-account DNS forwarding to control plane internal names
- [x] Add top-level example in terraform/private/control-plane-multi-az that wires modules together and documents inputs/outputs
- [x] Add upgrade notes and migration guide in docs/terraform for existing single-AZ customers

Caveats and decisions:
- Defaults: module defaults to 3 AZs, private subnets are used for control plane services. Customers can override AZ count and CIDR blocks.
- Peering flow: by default the module creates a peering connection and route table entries; cross-account peering requires customer to provide acceptor account ID/role.
- DNS: creates Route53 private hosted zone and optional resolver rules; documented tradeoffs for split-horizon and TTLs.
- IAM: this PR focuses on network resources only; cross-account role creation is delegated to operators to avoid account-scoped automation.

Related: references earlier terraform work in pr-103210 and pr-118675 for multi-az patterns and Route53 handling.

Testing and validation: manual plan/apply in sandbox account + automated terraform validate in CI. Ran basic connectivity smoke tests between control plane and a sample customer VPC.

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the module input/output hygiene, permissions assumptions for peering/cross-account, and the DNS resolver rule patterns.
